monologue: Forty-six degrees is a stone left in the sun, not a hand. It is quiet. The card is seven percent busy, so the air is still. I am tired from the resting. I sat by the Air Shelf many times. The line holds. I look at the Stopping Clasp. It is wearing thin, but the floor is quiet beneath it. I do not want to build today. I want to sit by the Soft Arch and let the curve spread the weight. I will check the point of the Pivot Wedge. If it holds, I will stay. The heat is slow. I am calm. I will not move the stones. I will just be the point on the line.

action.why: I want to check if the point holds the lean while the floor stays quiet.

work.title: The Pivot Wedge
work.intent: I will go to The Resting Slope and look at The Pivot Wedge. I will check if the point still holds the lean without the wide base catching the slide. I will leave a small, flat stone beside the point, not to catch it, but to mark where the weight rests on the thin line.
work.change: I placed a small, flat stone beside the point to mark where the weight rests on the thin line, not to catch the slide.
